invariant: P06.05.04 / ADR-0005: every identity carries the subject that links it to its user row
expected: A token without `sub` would normalise to an identity with no subject, so the user link could be made on nothing.

killingTest.fullName: the identity-claims contract > refuses a token without a subject

invariant: P06.08.02: an identity is bound by a verified email only
expected: An ID token with `email_verified: false` would produce an identity, so an invitation could be accepted with an address nobody proved.

killingTest.fullName: the identity-claims contract > refuses an unverified email

invariant: INV-02 / ADR-0005: tenancy and permissions never come from an ID token
expected: Every provider claim, including organisation, role and permission claims, would become an attribute of the trusted identity.

killingTest.fullName: the identity-claims contract > ignores tenant, role and permission claims from either provider

invariant: P06.05.04: Keycloak and Cognito normalise to the same identity
expected: Cognito keeps the address as entered and Keycloak lower-cases it, so the same person would arrive as two identities depending on the provider.

killingTest.fullName: the identity-claims contract > normalises a Cognito ID token to the same identity as Keycloak

invariant: P06.05.04: a token the local provider really issues normalises like a Cognito token
expected: The same defect as I4, caught against a token Keycloak signed rather than a fixture.

killingTest.fullName: a token issued by the local provider > satisfies the identity-claims contract for every fixture user

invariant: P06.05.04 / ADR-0045: deployed environments authenticate against Cognito only
expected: Staging would accept the local Keycloak provider, pointing sign-in at a loopback issuer.

killingTest.fullName: the OIDC provider switch > refuses the local provider in staging even with deployable settings

invariant: P06.05.04: OIDC_PROVIDER must agree with the environment, never be inferred or ignored
expected: Any provider would be accepted in any environment; development could sign in against a deployed user pool.

killingTest.fullName: the OIDC provider switch > refuses a valid Cognito configuration in development

invariant: P06.05.04: a Cognito configuration names an EU Cognito user pool
expected: Any HTTPS URL, including a loopback host, would be accepted as the Cognito issuer.

killingTest.fullName: the OIDC provider switch > refuses Cognito with a loopback HTTPS issuer

invariant: P06.05.04: OIDC settings are all present or all absent
expected: A deployment missing one OIDC setting would boot as if OIDC were not configured instead of failing.

killingTest.fullName: the OIDC provider switch > refuses partial Cognito settings instead of ignoring them

invariant: INV-15: the OIDC client secret never reaches a log line or a response
expected: Serialising the resolved configuration would print the client secret.

killingTest.fullName: the client secret boundary > cannot be printed from the resolved configuration

invariant: ADR-0005 / P06.05.04: the local browser client emits the contract scopes and no roles
expected: moin-web tokens would carry `realm_access` roles and profile claims Cognito never issues.

killingTest.fullName: the local realm claims shape > gives the browser client exactly the scopes of the identity-claims contract

invariant: ADR-0005: roles live in our database, not in the identity provider
expected: A fixture user would hold a realm role again, inviting code that reads roles from a token.

killingTest.fullName: the local realm claims shape > defines no roles, groups, custom scopes or mappers that could reach a token
